findings.claim: LSST is a dedicated telescope with an effective aperture of 6.7 meters and a field of view of 9.6 deg $^{2}$.

LSST will carry out a survey of 20,000 deg $^{2}$ of the sky in six broad photometric bands, imaging each region of sky roughly 2000 times (1000 pairs of back-to-back 15-sec exposures) over a ten-year survey lifetime.
The LSST project will deliver fully calibrated survey data to the United States scientific community and the public with no proprietary period.
The purpose of the LSST Science Book is to examine and document in detail science goals, opportunities, and capabilities that will be provided by the LSST.
The effective étendue for LSST will be $319 \, m^{2} deg^{2}$, more than an order of magnitude larger than that of any existing facility.

LSST is designed to achieve multiple goals in four main science themes: Taking an Inventory of the Solar System, Mapping the Milky Way, Exploring the Transient Optical Sky, and Probing Dark Energy and Dark Matter.
The LSST survey data will be public with no proprietary period in the United States, with a goal to make it world-public.
The combination of LSST with contemporary space-based near-infrared (NIR) missions will provide powerful synergies in studies of dark energy, galaxy evolution, and many other areas.

The baseline LSST cadence will result in orbital parameters for several million moving objects, dominated by main belt asteroids (MBAs), with light curves and colorimetry for a substantial fraction of detected objects.
The number of objects with documented orbits, colors, and variability information from LSST will represent an increase of factors of ten to one hundred over current numbers.
LSST will survey over half the celestial sphere for asteroids, get superb orbits, go tremendously faint, and measure precise colors, allowing measurement of light curves for thousands of TNOs.
LSST is the only ground-based survey that is capable of achieving the goal of cataloging 90% of all potentially hazardous asteroids larger than 140 meters in diameter.

LSST will enable studies of the distribution of numerous main sequence stars beyond the presumed edge of the Galaxy's halo, their metallicity distribution throughout most of the halo, and their kinematics beyond the thick disk/halo boundary
LSST will obtain direct distance measurements below the hydrogen-burning limit for a representative thin-disk sample

Compared to SDSS, LSST will cover an area more than twice as large, using hundreds of observations of the same region in a given filter instead of one or two, and each observation will be about two magnitudes deeper
LSST extends time-volume space a thousand times over current surveys.
LSST will enable the discovery and analysis of rare and exotic objects, such as neutron star and black hole binaries and high-energy transients.
LSST will characterize in detail active galactic nuclei (AGN) variability and new classes of transients, such as binary mergers and stellar disruptions by black holes.

LSST will provide a powerful new capability for monitoring periodic variables such as RR Lyrae stars, which will be used to map the Galactic halo and intergalactic space to distances exceeding 400 kpc.

LSST is unique in that its deep, wide-field, multi-color imaging survey can undertake four cosmic probes of dark matter and dark energy physics with a single data set and with much greater precision than previously.
By simultaneously measuring the redshift-distance relation and the growth of cosmic structure, LSST data can test whether the recent acceleration is due to dark energy or modified gravity.
The LSST system can adopt a highly efficient survey strategy where a single data set serves most science programs instead of science-specific surveys executed in series.

Having deeper data to treat as a model will reveal critical systematic uncertainties in the wider LSST survey, including photometric redshifts, that impact the measurements of weak lensing, clustering, galaxy morphologies, and galaxy luminosity functions.
The LSST optical design is a modified Paul-Baker three-mirror system with three refractive lenses and a color filter.
The LSST design is a generalization of the Mersenne-Schmidt family of designs.
The LSST has very low geometrical distortion with scale distortion less than 0.1% over the full FOV.
Direct drive systems were judged overly complicated and too excessive, so the LSST design has each motor working through a multi-stage gear reduction.
LSST photometric calibration is separated into three parts: relative calibration, absolute calibration of colors, and absolute calibration of flux.

The LSST strategy to measure the observational bandpass for each source is designed to reduce errors in the five color zero points to meet specifications in the survey requirements.

findings.claim: The system's ability to discern permanent binding and transient interaction allows studying the different interaction kinetics of zinc and mercury ions.
Detection of transient interactions enables statistical confirmation that sensor signals originate from single ions.
Mercury ions amalgamate with gold and zinc ions turn into probes of highly localized surface potentials as ionic strength evolves.
The technique detects single analyte molecules in the transient regime whereby no depletion via permanent binding occurs.

Performing the experiment under conditions that only allow for transient ion–NR interactions enables statistical confirmation of the single-ion nature of observed signals independently from the total number of available sensing sites.
The presence of additional electrolytes can give rise to mercury binding or changes in the transient behaviour of zinc ions.

For a permanent interaction, such as the formation of a strong covalent bond, the resonance will remain in this shifted position.

When an ion interacts with a NR in a way such that it only remains confined in a sensing site for a certain period of time, the resonance position is shifted back towards its original position after the ion leaves the sensing site.
Permanent interactions manifest as a step pattern, whereas transient interactions appear as fast changes that exhibit a spike pattern.
Events are identified based on deviations from the drift-free trace with a magnitude greater than 3σ, where σ is the standard deviation of the noise of the drift-free trace.
